resources.check: Ask about suitability, current places, charges and any referral or support arrangements.

resources.description: Find the local council route to apply for a council home or join the housing register.
resources.who: People looking for longer-term social housing; the council checks its local eligibility and priority rules.
resources.access: Enter a postcode on GOV.UK to find the council application route.
resources.check: There is usually a waiting list and a home is not guaranteed. If you have nowhere to stay now, contact the council’s homelessness team instead of relying on a register application.
resources.coverage: England; local council rules apply
resources.nextStep: Find your council’s housing register and check whether you can apply.

resources.name: Housing association homes — how to apply
resources.description: An overview of applying for housing association homes directly or through a council.
resources.who: People exploring longer-term housing association homes, often on a low income or needing additional support.
resources.access: Read the government guide, then contact the housing association or council to ask about its application process.
resources.check: Each provider sets eligibility and availability. You can apply to more than one association, but an application is not a guarantee of a home. This is not an emergency bed service.
resources.coverage: England; provider and council rules vary
resources.nextStep: Ask the council or housing association whether it accepts direct applications.

resources.name: Help with a rent deposit or rent in advance
resources.description: Understand possible council payments, local deposit schemes and other help to start a tenancy.
resources.who: People in England who cannot afford a deposit or rent in advance. Eligibility depends on the scheme.
resources.access: Read Shelter’s guide and use its postcode lookup to ask the council about housing or crisis payments and local deposit schemes.
resources.check: Help is not automatic. Some schemes offer grants; others involve loans or guarantees with conditions. Check repayment and other costs before agreeing.
resources.coverage: England
resources.nextStep: Ask the council about a local rent deposit or bond scheme and what you need to apply.

resources.name: Crisis Help to Rent — local private-renting schemes
resources.description: Find schemes that may help with finding a tenancy, deposit guarantees, rent in advance or keeping a home.
resources.who: People seeking help to access private rented housing; each local scheme has its own eligibility.
resources.access: Search the database by town, council area, county or region, then contact a listed scheme.
resources.check: Crisis says entries may not be fully current. Check availability and criteria with the scheme; the database does not allocate housing or award a deposit itself.
resources.coverage: UK
resources.nextStep: Find a local scheme and ask if it can help with your tenancy or deposit.

resources.name: Rethink — supported housing and mental illness
resources.description: A plain-language guide to housing with support, including how to ask for an assessment and plan housing after hospital.
resources.who: Adults aged 18+ living with mental illness in England, and their carers or loved ones.
resources.access: Read the guide. You can ask your mental health team about options or contact adult social care for a needs assessment.
resources.check: Supported housing access, referrals and charges vary. This information page does not offer an available placement or guarantee funding.
resources.coverage: England
resources.nextStep: Tell your care team what support you need at home and ask how to explore supported housing.

resources.name: Op FORTITUDE — housing support for veterans
resources.description: A national route for veterans who are homeless, may lose their home or need help keeping a tenancy.
resources.who: Single UK veterans facing homelessness or struggling to maintain their home. The provider assesses individual needs.
resources.access: Call free or use the online referral link. Veterans can contact the service themselves.
resources.check: The team assesses safety, housing needs and suitable support. Help depends on circumstances and available services; a housing place is not guaranteed.
resources.coverage: UK
resources.nextStep: Call 0800 952 0774 or start the online form and explain your current housing situation.

resources.name: HousingCare — retirement and sheltered housing finder
resources.description: Browse retirement, sheltered and extra-care housing by area and type.
resources.who: Older people and those helping someone explore housing options; each scheme sets its age and other criteria.
resources.access: Search the directory or choose an area, then contact a housing provider to ask about its application route.
resources.check: Listings are not a guarantee of a vacancy. Confirm age criteria, purchase or rent costs, service charges and care arrangements with the provider. This is a longer-term housing finder.
resources.coverage: UK
resources.nextStep: Choose an area and ask a listed provider about criteria, costs and vacancies.

resources.name: Civil Legal Advice — check legal aid and get advice
resources.description: Help to reach a legal adviser for eligible housing, debt, domestic abuse, discrimination and other civil problems.
resources.who: People in England or Wales whose problem and finances meet legal-aid rules.
resources.access: Use the GOV.UK legal-aid check, or contact CLA to explain the problem. Ask for a callback or an interpreter if needed.
resources.check: Legal advice is free if you qualify. Calls can cost money; a callback is available. An adviser checks eligibility and what help can be offered.
resources.coverage: England and Wales
resources.nextStep: Call CLA or use the eligibility check to find the right advice route.

resources.name: GOV.UK — find a legal adviser
resources.description: Find a solicitor or legal-aid adviser and understand free or lower-cost legal help.
resources.who: People looking for help with a legal problem; this guide explains the England and Wales system.
resources.access: Open the government guide and follow the legal-aid adviser finder for your postcode and problem.
resources.check: The adviser checks case and financial eligibility. Not every service is free, and availability varies. Confirm charges before agreeing to paid work.
resources.coverage: England and Wales; the guide links to separate Scottish and Northern Irish routes.
resources.nextStep: Choose the legal-aid or free-advice route on the guide, then contact an adviser.

resources.name: Law Centres Network — find a Law Centre
resources.description: Find local legal help with problems such as housing, benefits, employment and discrimination.
resources.who: People who need specialist legal help and may struggle to pay; each centre sets its own area and service rules.
resources.access: Choose a Law Centre from the list or map and contact that centre to ask whether it can help.
resources.check: Law Centres offer free legal help, but the legal topics, local coverage, casework and capacity differ. The network office is not an individual advice line.
resources.coverage: UK directory; each centre has its own local coverage.
resources.nextStep: Find the nearest centre and check that it covers your problem before visiting.

resources.name: LawWorks — free legal advice clinic finder
resources.description: Find a clinic for initial advice about housing, work, debt, benefits, family and other legal problems.
resources.who: People who cannot afford a lawyer and are not eligible for legal aid; individual clinics have extra criteria.
resources.access: Search by postcode, town, legal topic or appointment format, then contact the listed clinic.
resources.check: Advice is free. Many clinics provide an initial appointment rather than ongoing casework or representation. Check local coverage, eligibility and booking arrangements.
resources.coverage: England and Wales; clinic coverage varies.
resources.nextStep: Choose a clinic that covers your legal issue and ask for its next available appointment.

resources.name: Advocate — apply for free help from a barrister
resources.description: May find a volunteer barrister to advise, prepare legal arguments or represent someone in court.
resources.who: People with an England or Wales case who cannot afford a lawyer and cannot get legal aid or suitable legal-expenses insurance.
resources.access: Check eligibility, then complete the online application and provide the requested documents. A downloadable application is also available.
resources.check: Help depends on eligibility and volunteer availability. Normally allow at least three weeks after submitting a complete application; exceptional urgent cases have separate rules. No legal advice is given on the application phone line.
resources.coverage: Cases in England and Wales.
resources.nextStep: Read the eligibility and deadline rules before starting an application.

resources.name: Support Through Court — practical court support
resources.description: Help to understand court processes, organise papers and cope with a civil or family hearing.
resources.who: People facing civil or family court without a lawyer.
resources.access: Call the national helpline or book an online or local appointment through the website.
resources.check: Free practical and emotional support. Volunteers do not give legal advice or act as your lawyer. Check appointment availability.
resources.coverage: England and Wales.
resources.nextStep: Call the helpline and explain the hearing, paperwork or practical support you need.

resources.name: Rights of Women — legal advice lines
resources.description: Confidential legal advice about family issues, abuse, immigration, criminal justice and sexual harassment at work.
resources.who: Women seeking advice on the law in England and Wales.
resources.access: Choose the advice line for your issue on the website, then call during that line’s opening hours. Interpreting is available.
resources.check: Advice is free, but phone charges can apply. Different lines have different numbers and hours; voicemail does not take messages.
resources.coverage: England and Wales.
resources.nextStep: Choose family, immigration, criminal law or sexual-harassment advice and check its current phone hours.

resources.name: FLOWS — legal support for women facing domestic abuse
resources.description: Help to understand legal options for protection from domestic abuse and finding a suitable solicitor.
resources.who: Women affected by domestic abuse, with legal options in England and Wales.
resources.access: Call FLOWS or use its secure self-contact form to request a safe time for a response.
resources.check: Legal support is free. Legal aid and protective orders have their own rules. Contact FLOWS only when it is safe for you; it is not an emergency response service.
resources.sourceOwner: FLOWS — Finding Legal Options for Women Survivors
resources.coverage: England and Wales.
resources.nextStep: Contact FLOWS safely to discuss legal protection and the help available.

resources.name: Disability Law Service — legal advice
resources.description: Specialist help with disability-related housing, care, benefits, employment and discrimination problems.
resources.who: Disabled people and their carers; each advice service has its own scope and access rules.
resources.access: Choose your legal issue on the Free Advice page and use the current contact route for that team. Ask for communication adjustments as explained there.
resources.check: Advice is free. Subject, funding and area limits can apply, and replies may take several working days. Legal representation is a separate service with eligibility checks.
resources.coverage: Check the individual advice service’s area coverage.
resources.nextStep: Open the advice page and choose the housing, care, benefits or employment team.

resources.name: Equality Advisory and Support Service — discrimination and rights
resources.description: Help to understand discrimination, reasonable adjustments and ways to raise an equality or human-rights concern.
resources.who: People experiencing possible discrimination or human-rights problems in England, Scotland or Wales.
resources.access: Call the helpline, use chat or complete the contact form. The site explains BSL support.
resources.check: Free information and informal support. EASS does not give legal advice or represent people in court or a tribunal. It can help you look for legal assistance.
resources.coverage: England, Scotland and Wales.
resources.nextStep: Explain what happened and ask about the options for raising the concern.

resources.name: Mind Legal line — mental health rights
resources.description: Legal information about sectioning, mental capacity, community care, discrimination and equality.
resources.who: People asking about mental health-related law in England or Wales, including people supporting someone else.
resources.access: Call Mind’s Legal line or check the helplines page for current contact options.
resources.check: The line offers legal information and general advice. It does not provide representation, advocacy or ongoing casework. For benefits, housing or criminal-law questions, use a specialist advice service.
resources.coverage: England and Wales.
resources.nextStep: Call the Legal line with your mental-health-rights question.

resources.name: Advicenow — PIP decision challenge letter tool
resources.description: A guided tool to help draft a letter asking for a PIP decision to be looked at again.
resources.who: People challenging a Personal Independence Payment decision; the information applies to England and Wales.
resources.access: Read the guidance and use the mandatory-reconsideration letter tool. A free Advicenow account is needed to submit the tool form.
resources.check: The tool is free. Check your decision letter and current time limits. It helps draft a letter; it does not submit your challenge or provide individual representation.
resources.coverage: England and Wales; the provider also notes relevance for Northern Ireland.
resources.nextStep: Read the instructions, then use the guided tool to prepare your own letter.

resources.name: GOV.UK — appeal a benefit decision
resources.description: Official steps for taking a disputed benefit decision to an independent tribunal.
resources.who: People disputing eligible benefit or Child Maintenance decisions; different processes apply to Northern Ireland and Social Security Scotland.
resources.access: Check the government guide and your decision letter. It explains reconsideration, appeal forms and ways to get advice.
resources.check: Appealing is free, but time limits and procedural rules apply. Usually a reconsideration decision is needed first; the guide explains exceptions. Ask an adviser if you are unsure.
resources.sourceOwner: HM Courts and Tribunals Service — GOV.UK
resources.coverage: England, Wales and relevant Great Britain benefit appeals; separate routes are linked for Northern Ireland and Social Security Scotland.
resources.nextStep: Read your decision letter alongside the guide, and contact Citizens Advice if you need help.

resources.name: National Debtline — debt, bailiffs and court letters
resources.description: Free debt advice about bills, creditors, bailiffs and money-related court action.
resources.who: People with personal debt in England, Wales or Scotland.
resources.access: Call the helpline, use webchat or start the online advice tool. Choose the correct country on the website.
resources.check: Advice is free and confidential. Country-specific debt options have different rules; check current contact hours and discuss your situation with an adviser.
resources.coverage: England, Wales and Scotland.
resources.nextStep: Call or chat with an adviser and explain the bill, debt or letter you are worried about.

resources.name: GOV.UK — find a registered immigration adviser
resources.description: Find a regulated adviser for immigration, asylum or permission-to-stay questions.
resources.who: People needing qualified immigration advice about staying in the UK.
resources.access: Use the official guide and adviser finder. Check the adviser’s registration, area of work and charges before booking.
resources.check: The finder is free to use. Advice may be free or paid; application and translation costs can still apply. Advisers do not decide immigration applications.
resources.coverage: UK immigration advice.
resources.nextStep: Find a registered adviser and ask whether they can help with your issue and what it will cost.

resources.name: Family Rights Group — children’s services advice
resources.description: Independent advice to help families understand children’s social care processes, rights and options.
resources.who: Parents, kinship carers, relatives and friends of children who are involved with, or need help from, children’s services in England.
resources.access: Call the advice line or use the enquiry form, advice pages and family forums. Interpreters can be arranged.
resources.check: Advice is free and confidential. Email replies may take time. The service focuses on children’s services and related family processes, rather than all family-law problems.
resources.coverage: England.
resources.nextStep: Call the advice line and explain how children’s services are involved.

resources.name: Our Parks — Willesden Library yoga
resources.description: Gentle group yoga at Willesden Library, with movement adapted to different abilities.
resources.who: People wanting a gentle introduction or return to activity in Willesden.
resources.access: Register with Our Parks, then book a place from the Willesden Library timetable.
resources.check: Free. Check upcoming sessions and any access needs before attending.

resources.name: MoreYoga — Wembley Park studio
resources.description: Studio yoga with beginner classes, slower sessions and more active styles.
resources.who: People looking for yoga in Wembley Park.
resources.access: Use the Wembley Park timetable to choose and book a class.
resources.check: Paid classes and memberships. Check the full price, minimum commitment and cancellation terms.

resources.name: Re:Connect Studio — Queen’s Park hot yoga
resources.description: Independent studio offering hot yoga and other group movement classes in Queen’s Park.
resources.who: People interested in heated studio yoga near Queen’s Park and Kensal Rise.
resources.access: Book through the studio timetable or contact reception about a suitable first class.
resources.check: Paid. All classes use a heated room; check suitability, current prices and cancellation terms.

resources.name: Inner Space Wembley — free meditation
resources.description: Guided meditation, quiet reflection and self-development sessions from the Brahma Kumaris charity.
resources.who: Beginners and experienced meditators in Wembley; some sessions are also online.
resources.access: See the event calendar for current in-person and online sessions.
resources.check: Free; donations welcome. Sessions use the charity’s spiritual approach to meditation.
resources.coverage: 528 High Road, Wembley; selected online sessions.

resources.name: Global Co-operation House — meditation and quiet room
resources.description: Meditation courses, reflective activities and a quiet room in Willesden Green.
resources.who: People interested in the Brahma Kumaris approach to meditation and spiritual wellbeing.
resources.access: Browse the current programme or contact the centre about beginner courses and visiting.
resources.check: Activities are free, supported by donations. Check booking requirements for each event.

resources.name: Soham Yoga — yoga and meditation
resources.description: Community yoga and meditation with beginner, gentler and online options.
resources.who: People in Harrow, North Harrow and nearby areas; beginners welcome.
resources.access: Check the timetable or contact Soham about a suitable class.
resources.check: Paid classes and passes; ask about current concessions and community-funded places.

resources.name: Well Woman Yoga — Harrow Arts Centre
resources.description: Women-only group yoga with breathing, meditation and relaxation at Harrow Arts Centre.
resources.who: Women wanting an all-levels yoga class in Hatch End.
resources.access: Contact the teacher using the class page to ask about availability and book.
resources.check: Paid; the page lists drop-in and term prices. Confirm current timetable and any adaptations.

resources.name: Need to Talk — affordable counselling
resources.description: Charity counselling for adults, with individual, couple and family options.
resources.who: Adults in Harrow seeking help with emotional difficulties, relationships or life changes.
resources.access: Use “Apply for Counselling” on the contact page to ask about an assessment.
resources.check: Low-cost, paid service. Confirm the fee, session format and current availability; the postal address is not a session venue.

resources.name: DAWN Charitable Trust — multilingual counselling
resources.description: Culturally sensitive counselling in several languages, with women-only and gender-neutral appointment options.
resources.who: Harrow residents seeking individual, relationship or family counselling; ask about age and language options.
resources.access: Contact DAWN to discuss counselling, language needs and appointment options.
resources.check: Paid on a sliding scale; confirm fees and current availability. Women-only sessions run at specified times.

resources.name: Bereavement Care — listening and support groups
resources.description: Free one-to-one listening and groups where bereaved people can share their experiences.
resources.who: People and families affected by bereavement in Harrow, Hillingdon and nearby communities.
resources.access: Phone or use the contact form to discuss the support and local groups available.
resources.check: Free. Check the current group venue, access arrangements and availability.
resources.coverage: Harrow, Hillingdon and nearby communities; ask the charity which local group is suitable.

resources.name: Yoga with Anna — Ruislip classes
resources.description: Group yoga at The Stables in Ruislip, including options for beginners.
resources.who: People in Ruislip interested in group yoga; pregnancy-related options are also listed.
resources.access: Contact the teacher through the council listing to check the current class and book.
resources.check: Ask about fees, availability and a suitable class for your needs.

resources.name: Hotpod Yoga — Ruislip Manor
resources.description: Heated studio yoga with slower and more active class options.
resources.who: People aged 16+ interested in hot yoga in Ruislip Manor.
resources.access: Use the studio timetable to book; tell the teacher if it is your first visit.
resources.check: Paid. Heated to 37°C; the provider excludes pregnancy and under-16s and advises checking medical suitability when needed.

resources.name: MoreYoga — Uxbridge studio
resources.description: Studio yoga in central Uxbridge, with a choice of slower and more active styles.
resources.who: People looking for yoga near Uxbridge station.
resources.access: Check the Uxbridge timetable and book a suitable session online.
resources.check: Paid classes and memberships. Confirm the total cost, minimum commitment and cancellation terms before joining.
resources.coverage: 1–3 Bakers Road, Uxbridge.

resources.name: Mind in Hillingdon — free and paid counselling
resources.description: Individual counselling in Uxbridge or online, with free and paid access routes.
resources.who: Adults 18+. The free route has Hillingdon residency, GP and income criteria; the paid route accepts other areas.
resources.access: Read the two counselling options, then use the relevant self-referral form or phone for advice.
resources.check: The charity checks eligibility for free sessions. Paid assessment and sessions currently cost £40 each; check before applying.

resources.name: LINK — young people’s counselling
resources.description: One-to-one counselling online and in Hillingdon community settings.
resources.who: Young people aged 13–24 who live, work or study in Hillingdon and meet the programme criteria.
resources.access: Use the council’s targeted-programmes page to ask about LINK and the self-referral route.
resources.check: Free. The council checks suitability and consent; a place is confirmed after review.

resources.name: Harlington Hospice — counselling during serious illness
resources.description: Counselling for people facing a serious or terminal illness and those close to them.
resources.who: Adults 18+ living in Hillingdon or registered with a Hillingdon GP, affected by serious illness.
resources.access: Contact the hospice or follow its counselling page to ask about a self-referral.
resources.check: Free. Ask the team whether the service fits the person’s circumstances and about current availability.

resources.name: Ealing Yoga, Meditation and Philosophy Centre
resources.description: Charity classes combining yoga, breathing, relaxation and meditation at Ealing’s Friends Meeting House.
resources.who: People interested in yoga and meditation, including mixed-ability classes and beginners.
resources.access: Check the current class schedule or contact the centre about joining.
resources.check: Paid classes; ask about drop-in, course and member prices. Classes include spiritual and philosophical study.
resources.sourceOwner: Ealing Yoga, Meditation and Philosophy Centre

resources.name: Terri Yoga — Northfields and Ealing classes
resources.description: Group yoga indoors in Northfields, online and seasonally in local parks.
resources.who: People looking for group movement in Ealing; contact the teacher about a suitable level.
resources.access: Book a listed class or contact Terri to discuss joining.
resources.check: Paid. The teacher offers some free spaces when classes are not full for people unable to afford them; ask first.

resources.name: yoga-tastic — Pitshanger and Northfields
resources.description: Local yoga classes and beginner courses including breathing, relaxation and meditation.
resources.who: People seeking yoga in Pitshanger or Northfields, with an online class option.
resources.access: Contact the teacher to check the right class and current booking options.
resources.check: Paid, usually booked for a term. Ask about a trial or available drop-in place before paying.

resources.name: Ealing Abbey Counselling Service — low-cost therapy
resources.description: Charity counselling and psychotherapy with fees based on income.
resources.who: Adults seeking counselling. Priority is given to Ealing borough residents; neighbouring areas depend on capacity.
resources.access: Phone to discuss an assessment. If recently supported by a mental health team, ask that team about the written information required.
resources.check: Paid assessment and weekly sessions on a sliding scale. The service checks suitability and availability.

resources.name: Metanoia — low-cost counselling and psychotherapy
resources.description: Counselling and psychotherapy with supervised practitioners in training, in Ealing and online.
resources.who: People seeking an assessed low-cost talking therapy service.
resources.access: Use the clinic contact form, email or phone to ask about an initial assessment.
resources.check: Paid; assessment and session fees have reduced rates depending on circumstances. Ask about cost and availability.

resources.name: CAPE — therapy for complex mental health needs
resources.description: Charity psychotherapy and psychological support for people with long-term or complex mental health difficulties.
resources.who: Adults living in Ealing with severe or enduring mental health needs.
resources.access: Ask the care team about CAPE’s approved referral partners, or contact CAPE to understand access.
resources.check: CAPE currently accepts partner referrals only, not self-referrals. Check availability and any costs with the service.

resources.name: Living Well — HIV peer support and counselling
resources.description: Peer mentoring, counselling and wellbeing workshops for people living with or affected by HIV.
resources.who: Eligible Ealing residents affected by HIV; the team can explain funded access.
resources.access: Phone or use “Sign Up” on the provider website to discuss the support available.
resources.check: Free for eligible residents. Ask about current options, access criteria and session format.

resources.name: Asian Family Counselling Service — Southall
resources.description: Culturally sensitive individual, couple and family counselling in several South Asian languages.
resources.who: South Asian people aged over 16, including couples where one partner is South Asian.
resources.access: Contact the Southall office by phone or email to discuss an appointment.
resources.check: Low-cost paid service. Confirm the fee, language, session format and current availability.

resources.name: Bereft — bereavement counselling
resources.description: Charity counselling offering space to talk through grief after someone has died.
resources.who: People aged 16+ living in the London Borough of Ealing.
resources.access: Phone the team or use the assessment questions linked from the contact page.
resources.check: A per-session donation is requested according to what you can afford; inability to donate does not exclude someone. Ask about availability.

resources.name: Women + Health — counselling and wellbeing
resources.description: A Camden charity offering talking therapies, yoga, relaxation and community wellbeing sessions.
resources.who: Adults; most services are for women, with some designated services for men. Ask which sessions are suitable.
resources.access: Use the booking page or contact the team; counselling enquiries can go to counselling@women-and-health.org.
resources.check: Paid counselling uses a sliding scale. Group activities may be free, low cost or donation based; check the session price and current venue.

resources.name: CPU London — charitable psychotherapy
resources.description: Individual and group psychotherapy for Londoners who cannot afford private treatment.
resources.who: Adults across London on low incomes or benefits; dedicated funded places also support people aged 18–25.
resources.access: Phone the charity to ask about its application process and current places; people can contact it themselves.
resources.check: Free and supported places depend on assessment and availability. Sessions are mainly in person in Camden or Islington and involve a regular commitment.

resources.name: Highgate Counselling Centre
resources.description: A charity offering individual, couple and family counselling in Highgate and online.
resources.who: Individuals, couples and families seeking counselling.
resources.access: Read Getting started and complete the registration forms, or contact the centre for help.
resources.check: An initial consultation has a charge; ongoing contributions are agreed using income and circumstances. Ask about current fees, availability and access needs.

resources.name: The Gestalt Centre — low-cost therapy
resources.description: Weekly counselling and psychotherapy with supervised senior trainees, in Camden or online.
resources.who: People on lower incomes who would struggle to pay private therapy fees.
resources.access: Use the low-cost therapy form or email therapy.scheme@gestaltcentre.org.uk.
resources.check: Paid service: published fees are £25–£50 per session. Places are limited, with a waiting list and a weekly commitment. Ask whether the service fits the person’s needs.

resources.name: Brandon Centre — young-adult counselling
resources.description: Free counselling and psychotherapy with a charity supporting young people in Camden and Islington.
resources.who: People aged 16–24 who live or have a GP in Camden or Islington.
resources.access: Phone or email counselling@brandoncentre.org.uk to ask for the self-referral form. Help completing paperwork is available.
resources.check: Free, subject to assessment and availability. Ask about in-person or video sessions and access requirements.

resources.name: Brandon Centre — Mindful Movers yoga
resources.description: A six-week group programme combining yoga and relaxation for young people.
resources.who: Young people aged 16–24 in Camden and Islington; people aged 25 should check with the team.
resources.access: Email yoga@brandoncentre.org.uk to ask about the next group or use the young person’s sign-up form.
resources.check: A funded programme with termly groups. Confirm costs, venue, suitability and available spaces. Published age limits vary, so check with the team if aged 25.

resources.name: HOME Wellness — Primrose Hill yoga
resources.description: A paid studio offering yoga, Pilates, tai chi and wellbeing classes in Primrose Hill.
resources.who: People looking for studio classes, including options at different levels.
resources.access: Browse the class timetable and book through the website; ask reception for a suitable first class.
resources.check: Paid classes and memberships. Check current prices, class level and cancellation terms; concessions for some younger participants are advertised.

resources.name: MoreYoga — Kentish Town
resources.description: A yoga studio at Holmes Studios with slower, restorative, beginner and more active class options.
resources.who: People interested in paid yoga classes in Kentish Town.
resources.access: Choose a suitable class on the local timetable and book online.
resources.check: Paid studio. Introductory membership offers have ongoing charges and minimum terms; check the full price and cancellation rules before paying.

resources.name: Yoga with Charli — Belsize and Hampstead
resources.description: Small group yoga at Belsize Community Library and the RFC Rec Club, with some online options.
resources.who: Adults seeking local yoga; slower beginner and mixed-level classes are listed.
resources.access: View class levels and book a place through the website; contact the teacher about suitability or access.
resources.check: Paid classes, with single sessions and class packs. Check current prices, venue and cancellation rules.

resources.name: Likewise — community wellbeing programme
resources.description: A community hub offering friendly activities, creative groups, cooking, gardening and occasional wellbeing days.
resources.who: Adults aged 18+ looking for connection and wellbeing activities in Camden.
resources.access: Check the activity programme or call 020 7278 4437. Drop-in sessions do not require advance registration; other activities may need a place booked.
resources.check: Most activities are free. Confirm the timetable and any costs; the separate one-to-one support service has its own access process.

resources.name: Mind in Camden — free peer support groups
resources.description: Facilitated groups where people share experiences of anxiety, low mood or hearing voices; a women’s hearing-voices group is also available.
resources.who: Adults, including people who do not live in Camden. A diagnosis is not required.
resources.access: Use the group joining form or email phoenix@mindincamden.org.uk to discuss the right group before attending.
resources.check: Free. Check which groups have spaces: some groups may be full. Peer support is different from talking therapy.

resources.name: CCIWBS — bereavement counselling
resources.description: A charity offering individual and group bereavement counselling, with separate grief walks for social connection.
resources.who: Bereaved adults; funded counselling is listed for people living or working in Camden and Islington, with paid routes for the City and Westminster.
resources.access: Phone to discuss the available service or use its individual or group application form.
resources.check: Individual counselling applications start six months after the death; group counselling starts after 12 months. Free and paid places depend on area, funding and assessment.
resources.sourceOwner: Camden City Islington and Westminster Bereavement Service

resources.name: The Caravan — free listening and counselling
resources.description: A charity drop-in offering a listening space and emotional support, with counselling by arrangement.
resources.who: Adults seeking someone to talk to, in Piccadilly or by phone.
resources.access: Visit the green caravan at St James’s Church, Piccadilly, or phone the service. No advance booking for the initial drop-in.
resources.check: Free; donations are welcome. Check opening times and physical access. You may need to wait or try again when a counsellor is available.
resources.sourceOwner: The Caravan / Centre for Counselling and Psychotherapy Education

resources.name: CCPE — low-cost counselling clinic
resources.description: Weekly counselling and psychotherapy with supervised trainees through a charitable education centre in Little Venice.
resources.who: Adults aged 18+ who want to explore lower-cost therapy.
resources.access: Email info@ccpe.org.uk to request an assessment for the low-cost clinic.
resources.check: Paid service: the published low-cost assessment is £30, with weekly fees from £35. Confirm fees, availability and whether the service is suitable.
resources.sourceOwner: Centre for Counselling and Psychotherapy Education

resources.name: Iyengar Yoga London — Maida Vale
resources.description: A charitable yoga centre with beginner courses, studio and online classes, and concession places.
resources.who: Beginners and experienced adults; different classes have different experience or age requirements.
resources.access: Use the beginner course or class timetable to book, or contact the centre about a first class and concessions.
resources.check: Paid classes. Selected open-access classes have concession prices for eligible visitors without membership; proof of eligibility is required. Check current details.

resources.name: Indaba Yoga — Marylebone
resources.description: A paid yoga studio offering in-person and online classes in a range of styles.
resources.who: People seeking yoga in Marylebone; ask about a suitable level before booking.
resources.access: Browse the schedule and book online; email welcome@indabayoga.com with questions.
resources.check: Paid classes, packs and memberships. Check the current price and minimum term; some memberships have cancellation charges.

resources.name: West London Buddhist Centre — meditation and yoga
resources.description: Meditation drop-ins, courses and yoga at an accessible Royal Oak centre, plus some online sessions.
resources.who: People of any faith or no faith, including beginners.
resources.access: Choose a drop-in or course from the calendar; book yoga through the yoga page or ask the centre for advice.
resources.check: Meditation classes are donation based; courses use a sliding scale. Yoga and workshops have separate prices. Ask about affordability and access needs.

resources.name: Marylebone Psychodynamic — low-cost clinic
resources.description: Weekly psychodynamic psychotherapy with supervised trainees, in central London or online.
resources.who: Adults seeking a lower-cost regular therapy option.
resources.access: Contact the practice for an initial telephone conversation; people can approach the service themselves.
resources.check: Paid therapy and assessment, with fees agreed by income. Check current fees, suitability and availability before committing to weekly sessions.

resources.name: Allkind RISE — low-cost counselling
resources.description: A mental health charity’s talking therapy service, with appointments in Westminster or online.
resources.who: Adults aged 18+ across London. The service assesses whether its support is suitable.
resources.access: Use the service’s self-contact form or email risecounselling@allkind.org.uk; phone for help deciding whether to apply.
resources.check: Paid: £50 assessment, then £35 or £45 per session. RISE lists limits including current or past psychosis, specialist needs and therapy elsewhere; discuss fit with the team.

resources.name: The Life Centre — Notting Hill yoga
resources.description: A paid yoga and Pilates studio offering classes and wellbeing workshops in Notting Hill.
resources.who: Beginners and experienced participants seeking studio or live online classes.
resources.access: Choose a suitable class and book online, or contact reception for help.
resources.check: Paid. Concessions are advertised on some class packs for eligible groups; check current prices, proof needed and membership terms.

resources.name: Sangyé Yoga — community and studio classes
resources.description: Yoga and meditation in North Kensington, including a free or donation-based community class alongside paid sessions.
resources.who: People seeking yoga, including beginner-level classes; ask which session is suitable.
resources.access: Use the online timetable to book, or contact the studio about its community class.
resources.check: Community class is free or by optional donation. Other classes are paid, with some concessions; confirm the current timetable and prices.

resources.name: Help Counselling — affordable talking therapy
resources.description: A charity offering short- and longer-term counselling in west London and online.
resources.who: Adults aged 18+; no GP referral is needed to contact the service.
resources.access: Contact the client team or use the website to ask about counselling and an assessment.
resources.check: Paid, with income-based fees and some concessions. Check the current session fee, location and suitability; this is not an urgent service.

resources.name: Yogalily Studio — yoga, Tai Chi and Qigong
resources.description: Yoga, Pilates, Tai Chi and Qigong classes in Milton Keynes, including beginner courses and chair-based Tai Chi.
resources.who: People seeking studio or online movement classes; ask which class fits your needs.
resources.access: Use the timetable to book, or contact the studio about beginners and chair-based sessions.
resources.check: Paid classes. Check current prices, access needs and cancellation terms before booking.

resources.name: Elli Yoga — Bow Brickhill community yoga
resources.description: Small group yoga classes at Bow Brickhill Community Hall, with options to take part at your own pace.
resources.who: People looking for a small, informal yoga class in Milton Keynes.
resources.access: Book a class on the website, or email info@elli.yoga with questions before attending.
resources.check: Paid classes. Check current price, venue access and the next available session.

resources.name: Moon and Stars Yoga — Stony Stratford
resources.description: Group Vinyasa and restorative yoga, including beginner-friendly sessions in Stony Stratford.
resources.who: People seeking a local group yoga class, including beginners.
resources.access: Use the yoga lessons page or contact the teacher to book and confirm the current venue.
resources.check: Paid classes. Confirm price, timetable and suitability before booking; sessions may use scented oils and candles.

resources.name: Poplar Osteopathy Clinic — yoga classes in Bletchley
resources.description: Mixed-ability group yoga and individual yoga sessions in Bletchley.
resources.who: People able to get up and down from the floor unaided; contact the teacher about kneeling or access needs.
resources.access: Book through the yoga page or phone the clinic to discuss a suitable class.
resources.check: Paid classes. Check current fees. The group includes floor work and kneeling; ask before attending if this is difficult.

resources.name: Samatha Meditation Centre — Great Holm
resources.description: Group breathing meditation classes in a Buddhist tradition, with sessions for beginners.
resources.who: New and experienced meditators; people under 18 need written parental consent.
resources.access: Contact the teacher named beside the relevant class on the website before joining.
resources.check: No fixed charge; donations welcome. Check course start dates and ask about sitting on a chair if needed.

resources.name: West Bletchley Wellbeing & Counselling Service
resources.description: Community counselling for issues such as stress, loss, relationships and life changes.
resources.who: Residents of West Bletchley, Bletchley and Fenny Stratford council areas, with paid options for other Milton Keynes residents.
resources.access: Phone or use the contact form to ask about counselling and the route for your council area.
resources.check: No charge for residents of the named council areas; paid options elsewhere. The service checks suitability and availability.

resources.name: The Man Cave UK — men’s peer support in Milton Keynes
resources.description: Volunteer-led talking groups where men share experiences and support each other. Meetings are listed for central Milton Keynes, Newport Pagnell and Bletchley.
resources.who: People who identify as men, aged over 18.
resources.access: Check the current meeting page, then attend an open meeting. No registration or professional referral is needed.
resources.check: No attendance fee; donations welcome. This is mutual peer support, rather than counselling. Check times and venue access first.

resources.name: Rethink — Recovery College Community Inclusion Service
resources.description: Community support and wellbeing hubs, with activities such as yoga, walking, arts, cooking and mindfulness.
resources.who: Adults experiencing mental distress in Milton Keynes; carers can take part in some activities.
resources.access: Email rccis@rethink.org to ask about current wellbeing hubs, access drop-ins and any entry requirements.
resources.check: Ask which activities are open to you, whether booking or assessment is needed, and any costs. Individual support has a separate access process.

resources.name: Willen Hospice — bereavement support
resources.description: Bereavement support that may include facilitated groups, support phone calls or counselling.
resources.who: People whose loved one was cared for by Willen Hospice.
resources.access: Call the Psychology and Counselling team or use the hospice’s online request form to discuss support.
resources.check: The hospice checks what support it can offer. Ask about current availability, any costs and group arrangements.

resources.name: Vayu Yoga — Guildford studio
resources.description: Yoga and Pilates classes, beginner courses and workshops at an independent Guildford studio.
resources.who: Beginners and experienced participants; check individual class styles and access.
resources.access: Use the timetable to book or contact info@vayu-yoga.co.uk about a suitable class.
resources.check: Paid classes and courses. Check current prices, venue access and cancellation terms before booking.

resources.name: GuildfordYoga — Guildford, Bramley and online
resources.description: Small mixed-ability yoga classes in community venues, with online sessions also listed.
resources.who: People looking for mixed-ability yoga in Guildford or Bramley, or online.
resources.access: Check the weekly timetable, book online or contact the teacher about pay-as-you-go and concessions.
resources.check: Paid classes; concessions may be available. Check the timetable for term breaks and confirm venue access.

resources.name: YogaShala — Buckland Park Lake
resources.description: Yoga classes near Reigate, including a beginner course and mixed yoga sessions beside Buckland Park Lake.
resources.who: Beginners and other people seeking yoga classes near Reigate and Dorking.
resources.access: Choose a class on the website and use its booking link; ask the teacher if unsure which session to try.
resources.check: Check the current course or drop-in charge, access and booking terms. Places and beginner-course dates vary.

resources.name: Yoga with Jasma — Guildford Institute
resources.description: Small group Hatha-based yoga classes with movement, breathing and guided relaxation.
resources.who: People seeking local yoga, including beginners; check the class level with the teacher.
resources.access: Email namaste@yogawithjasma.co.uk or use the class page to ask about places and booking.
resources.check: Paid classes. Confirm the current price, venue access and what equipment to bring.

resources.name: Sarra Yoga — Cranleigh and online
resources.description: Iyengar yoga classes, including beginner and slower-paced sessions at Cranleigh venues and online.
resources.who: Beginners and other yoga participants; older beginners are welcomed in named slower-paced classes.
resources.access: Choose a class on the timetable or email sarra@sarrayoga.co.uk for booking help.
resources.check: Paid classes. Confirm the class level, location, current price and any access needs before booking.

resources.name: The Counselling Partnership — affordable counselling
resources.description: Charitable one-to-one counselling in North Surrey and online.
resources.who: Adults aged 18 and over; not a couples or under-18 service.
resources.access: Contact the charity through its enquiry form, email or phone. No GP referral is needed.
resources.check: Contributions are requested, including an initial consultation charge. Discuss reduced contributions if on a low income; confirm costs before starting.

resources.name: Connect Counselling — Camberley
resources.description: Charitable individual counselling, offered face to face in Camberley or online.
resources.who: People seeking individual counselling; the charity checks suitability at an initial appointment.
resources.access: Use the website’s “Refer Yourself” form or phone to ask about counselling.
resources.check: Subsidised fees reflect financial circumstances. Agree the assessment and ongoing fees before starting.

resources.name: DHC Talking Therapies — NHS Surrey
resources.description: NHS talking therapy options including individual support, group courses and guided online CBT.
resources.who: People aged 17 and over registered with a Surrey GP.
resources.access: Call DHC or follow its self-referral route to request support yourself. A GP referral is not required.
resources.check: Free NHS service. The team assesses which support fits; contact them about access needs and current availability.

resources.name: PeerTalk — Guildford and Farnham support groups
resources.description: Charity peer groups for sharing experiences of depression, anxiety and emotional distress, facilitated by trained volunteers.
resources.who: Adults aged 18 and over.
resources.access: Check the current Guildford or Farnham meeting details and turn up. No appointment or referral is needed.
resources.check: Free peer support. You can listen without sharing. Check venue and time before travelling; older directories may show a previous Guildford venue.

resources.name: HeartBeat Support Woking
resources.description: Peer support, talks and social events for people affected by heart problems in Woking and nearby areas.
resources.who: People with heart problems, with partners, carers, family and interested local residents welcomed.
resources.access: Use the contact page or membership details to ask about the next meeting.
resources.check: Small meeting admission charges apply. Venues vary by season; confirm the current location and access needs.

resources.name: The Brigitte Trust — bereavement support groups
resources.description: Structured bereavement groups with a professional facilitator and opportunities to share experiences with others.
resources.who: People in Surrey struggling with grief.
resources.access: Contact the service manager to register interest in a group you can reach.
resources.check: Free courses. Places are limited, and locations and start dates vary; check the next available group.

resources.name: Headway Surrey — online coffee mornings
resources.description: Informal Zoom coffee mornings for people living with brain injury to chat and share experiences.
resources.who: Brain injury survivors living in Surrey; family members and carers are also welcomed.
resources.access: Contact Headway Surrey for the joining link and next online session.
resources.check: Free online coffee mornings. A device and internet access are needed; you can join in or listen quietly. Other Headway services may have fees.

resources.name: NHS — find talking therapies
resources.description: Find the local NHS service for anxiety and depression and its self-contact route.
resources.who: People in England aged 18 and over; some areas accept ages 16–17.
resources.access: Use the NHS finder with the person’s GP surgery, then check the local service’s contact options. The person can contact it themselves.
resources.check: Free NHS service. An assessment decides suitability; waiting times vary. A caller can help find the contact without making a professional referral.
resources.coverage: England; local access criteria apply.

resources.name: BACP — counsellor and therapist finder
resources.description: Search registered or accredited BACP therapists by location and the support wanted.
resources.who: People exploring private counselling or psychotherapy in the UK.
resources.access: Search the directory, read a therapist’s profile and contact them directly.
resources.check: Browsing is free. Therapy is usually paid; ask about fees, reduced rates, accessibility and availability before booking.
resources.sourceOwner: British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: UKCP — psychotherapist finder
resources.description: Find UKCP-accredited psychotherapists offering in-person, online or telephone sessions.
resources.who: People seeking private psychotherapy, with different ages and needs covered by individual practitioners.
resources.access: Search by postcode, issue, language or session type and contact the practitioner.
resources.check: Private therapy is usually paid. Ask about current fees and any lower-cost places; the directory does not book or fund sessions.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: BAATN — Black, African, Asian and Caribbean therapist finder
resources.description: Find counsellors, psychotherapists and psychologists of Black, African, Asian and Caribbean heritage.
resources.who: People looking for culturally informed therapy and a therapist from these heritage groups.
resources.access: Search by location or specialism and use the individual therapist’s contact details.
resources.check: Directory access is free. Practitioners set their own fees; ask about reduced rates, qualifications and current availability.
resources.sourceOwner: The Black, African and Asian Therapy Network
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: Pink Therapy — LGBTQ+ affirmative therapist finder
resources.description: Find therapists who work with gender, sexuality and relationship diversity.
resources.who: LGBTQ+ people and others seeking gender, sex and relationship diversity affirmative therapy.
resources.access: Use Find a Therapist on the website, then contact a practitioner directly.
resources.check: Independent practitioners charge their own fees. Check fees, qualifications, concessions and availability before booking.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: Free Psychotherapy Network — low-income therapy directory
resources.description: A network of therapists offering some no-fee psychotherapy places for people on low incomes.
resources.who: People on low incomes or benefits seeking psychotherapy.
resources.access: Choose a therapist from the geographical directory and contact them to ask whether a free place is available.
resources.check: Free places are limited and not guaranteed. Check professional registration, location or online options and any waiting list with the therapist.
resources.coverage: UK directory; coverage and no-fee vacancies vary by therapist.

resources.name: Anxiety UK — talking therapy and support groups
resources.description: A charity offering online talking therapy and groups to share experiences of anxiety.
resources.who: Adults over 18 seeking anxiety therapy; check the audience for each support group.
resources.access: Explore the therapy application or the anxiety support group booking links on the charity’s website.
resources.check: Paid membership and therapy fees apply. Therapy fees depend on household income. Group access can depend on membership; check the chosen booking and costs.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: OCD Action — online peer-support groups
resources.description: Volunteer-led groups for sharing experiences of OCD and related conditions.
resources.who: UK residents affected by OCD or related conditions, including loved ones; age and theme vary by group.
resources.access: Choose an open group and complete the website’s sign-up form. Sessions use Zoom; cameras can be off.
resources.check: Free. No formal diagnosis is required. Some groups are full and registration is checked before joining.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: OCD-UK — online peer-support meetings
resources.description: Online groups to talk with others affected by OCD, with general and themed sessions.
resources.who: UK residents with OCD and adult family members or friends. The main open groups are for ages 18 and over.
resources.access: Choose a meeting and register in advance. A Zoom account is required to register and attend.
resources.check: Free; paid OCD-UK membership is not required. Places are limited, and themed groups have their own age or audience rules.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: Beat — eating-disorder online support groups
resources.description: Moderated text-chat groups for people affected by eating disorders, with different groups for different experiences.
resources.who: People in the UK who have or think they may have an eating disorder; no formal diagnosis is required.
resources.access: Choose a group on the website and read its joining and chat-room guidance.
resources.check: Check the current group timetable and age rules. These are peer-support chats; ask Beat about any access or cost questions.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: Mind — Side by Side online community
resources.description: A moderated online space to share mental-health experiences and offer mutual support.
resources.who: People over 18 who want online connection around mental health.
resources.access: Register on Side by Side, choose a username and read the community guidelines.
resources.check: Free online community. Registration is needed. It does not provide emergency support or a personal therapy service.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: BDD Foundation — online BDD peer group
resources.description: A user-led Zoom group to share experiences of body dysmorphic disorder.
resources.who: People affected by body dysmorphic disorder; ask the organiser about any age or joining requirements.
resources.access: Email support@bddfoundation.org to register for the BDD Foundation’s own group. The page also lists other organisers’ groups.
resources.check: National Lottery funded; confirm any cost when registering. Camera use is optional. Check the current meeting dates.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: HoardingUK — online support for hoarding
resources.description: Groups to share experiences of hoarding, alongside groups for family and friends.
resources.who: People with hoarding behaviours and people supporting someone who hoards.
resources.access: Choose an online group from the charity’s support-groups page and follow its booking link.
resources.check: Some sessions are free; Place in the Space requests a £5 donation, with a published waiver if unable to pay. Places can be full; check the booking.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: The Loss Foundation — cancer-bereavement support groups
resources.description: Facilitated groups where people bereaved by cancer can talk, listen and connect.
resources.who: Adults affected by cancer bereavement; choose a group for the relevant loss or age group.
resources.access: Choose a support-group event from the calendar and register for the joining details.
resources.check: Free. Online and some in-person events are available. Check the event’s audience and availability. There is no pressure to speak.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: WAY Widowed and Young — bereavement peer community
resources.description: Peer groups, local meetups and an online community after the death of a partner.
resources.who: People who were aged 50 or under when their partner died, married or unmarried, with or without children.
resources.access: Read the membership information and apply online. Ask about financial support with membership if needed.
resources.check: Paid annual membership is £30 at the check date. Financial help may be available. Check any separate event costs.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: The Compassionate Friends — bereaved-parent community
resources.description: A private forum where bereaved parents can share experiences and support each other.
resources.who: Bereaved parents over 18 after the death of a child from one month old through adulthood.
resources.access: Use the forum registration link. The charity’s team checks registration before access.
resources.check: Check the forum rules and any cost questions with the charity. Other support for siblings and grandparents has separate access routes.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: Long Covid UK — online peer community
resources.description: Volunteer-moderated groups for people with Long Covid and those close to them, plus online activities.
resources.who: People living with Long Covid and their family or other close supporters.
resources.access: Follow the support-group links on the charity’s website and answer the Facebook group joining questions.
resources.check: A Facebook account is required for the main groups. Check any activity costs and access needs. In-person groups are only in specified locations.
resources.coverage: Online groups are accessible across the UK; in-person groups have limited local coverage.

resources.name: Endometriosis UK — local and online peer groups
resources.description: Groups and an online community for sharing experiences of endometriosis.
resources.who: People affected by endometriosis. Under-16s must attend support groups with an adult.
resources.access: Find a local group and join its mailing list, or use the website’s online support options.
resources.check: Check meeting format, access and any cost with the group. Some use private Facebook groups; online options are listed for people without a local group.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: Ehlers-Danlos Support UK — EDS and HSD peer groups
resources.description: Volunteer-led local and online groups for meeting others with EDS or hypermobility spectrum disorders.
resources.who: UK patients with EDS or HSD and their families.
resources.access: Join the charity’s community, then find a regional group and check its meeting details.
resources.check: Basic membership is free and includes access to support groups. Paid membership options are also offered. Check event access and any extra costs.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: PTSD Resolution — veterans and family therapy
resources.description: A charity offering free therapy through its therapist network, with local and remote appointments.
resources.who: UK armed-forces veterans, reservists and their families.
resources.access: Contact the charity or use its Register for Help form to discuss eligibility and options.
resources.check: Free for eligible beneficiaries; the service checks suitability and availability. The person can make direct contact. It is not an emergency service.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: Combat Stress — veterans’ peer-support network
resources.description: A developing network of veteran-led online and in-person peer groups for connection and shared recovery experiences.
resources.who: Veterans seeking connection around mental health, including those not receiving Combat Stress treatment.
resources.access: Email peersupport@combatstress.org.uk to ask about current groups, or browse the Veterans Recovery Network page.
resources.check: Combat Stress treatment is not required. The network is developing and event listings are being planned; ask the team what is currently available and about any costs.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: NHS — yoga, Pilates and meditation at home
resources.description: Free videos to try yoga, Pilates and meditation at home, including chair-based and pregnancy-related options.
resources.who: People wanting home activities; select a video appropriate to the person’s circumstances.
resources.access: Choose a video on the NHS website and read its suitability guidance before starting.
resources.check: Free. Read the specific video’s health and exercise guidance; seek advice if unsure about suitability after illness, injury or pregnancy.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: Mental Health Foundation — short mindfulness audio
resources.description: A free three-minute guided breathing-space recording to try at home.
resources.who: People who would like a short, self-guided mindfulness activity.
resources.access: Play the recording from the charity’s website.
resources.check: Free. This is a recorded wellbeing exercise; no group booking or counselling is provided. Stop if it feels uncomfortable.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

resources.name: The Free Mindfulness Project — guided recordings
resources.description: A collection of guided mindfulness, breathing and body-scan recordings to listen to or download.
resources.who: People looking for self-guided mindfulness resources rather than a live group.
resources.access: Choose a recording on the website or use its free audio-player web app.
resources.check: Free to access. Recordings vary in length and style. This resource does not provide individual assessment or talking therapy.
resources.coverage: UK-wide online or directory access; check the chosen service.

directoryRelease.sourceNote: Yoga, meditation, charitable talking therapies and peer-support access checked against provider and official pages. Costs, locality limits and direct-contact routes are recorded. Earlier check dates retained for unchanged records.
directoryRelease.audienceIndexNote: Audience filters use the groups explicitly named in each listing, intended users or recorded tags. They do not imply exclusive eligibility. Everyone shows all listings. General services are not duplicated under every audience.

searchRelease.method: Local keyword and common-needs matching, with optional AI interpretation only after an explicit request. Icon and area filters run locally.
searchRelease.nationalScope: Verified national options accompany selected local areas for practical support, talking therapies, peer support, yoga and relaxation.
